- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.20) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust for recent sentiment shifts or price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope after spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows — dampen extremes by smoothing with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise — use sentiment-weighted smoothing or ignore sentiment if >0.20 or < -0.20 for 2+ consecutive days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates late-period prices — reduce final 5–7 days by 1–2% per day if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
